facts.label: Passado e desejos
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para o que você fez: I went to a class. Use I’d like to + verbo para dizer o que você gostaria de fazer: I’d like to make a bowl.

facts.label: Passado simples
facts.sub: Para falar do passado, verbos regulares terminam em -ed: started, looked, loved. Verbos irregulares mudam: go vira went, make vira made.

facts.label: Perguntas no passado
facts.sub: Para perguntar sobre o passado, use did + verbo base: Did you make something? Why did you choose pottery? Não coloque o verbo no passado depois de did.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The past of make is maked.
“I’d like to try” means I want to try.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Regular past verbs end in -ed. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
The past of make is maked. → Falso (It is made.)
“I’d like to try” means I want to try. → Verdadeiro (Yes, politely.)

pages.title: A bright art room · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Monday afternoon in a bright art room in Dallas. Shelves hold cups, bowls and small plates. Grace cleans a table near the window. Her friend Max comes in with a paper bag. His hands are gray with dry clay. Grace smiles and asks about him.
“Hi, Max! What did you do last weekend?” says Grace. “I started a new hobby. I went to a pottery class.” says Max. “Wow! Why did you choose pottery?” says Grace.

pages.what: O -ed soa de três formas: “t” em looked, “d” em loved e “id” em wanted. I’d soa “aid”.
